item.title: [UPDATED] If you see Error 3194, Error 1109, or other network connectivity errors when restoring your iPhone or iPad

-- This device isn't eligible for the requested build.
+- Error: This device isn't eligible for the requested build.
-If you see one of these messages and need help updating or restoring your iOS or iPadOS device, make sure your Mac is up to date.
-
-If you're using iTunes, [install the latest version of iTunes](https://support.apple.com/en-us/118290) and try to update or restore your device again. If you're using Apple Devices on your PC, make sure you [use the latest version](https://support.apple.com/en-us/118406) . If you still can't update or restore, follow the steps below.
+If you're using iTunes, [install the latest version of iTunes](https://support.apple.com/en-us/118290) and update or restore your device again. If you're using the Apple Devices app on your PC, make sure that you [update to the latest version](https://support.apple.com/en-us/118406) .
-If you have a firewall or security software installed on your computer, they might block access to some Apple software update servers. Try these steps:
+A firewall or security software installed on your computer might block access to our software update servers.
-- [Be sure you have a working Internet connection](https://support.apple.com/en-us/101181) . Try visiting [www.apple.com](https://www.apple.com/) or contact your Internet service provider for more help.
+- [Check your Internet connection](https://support.apple.com/en-us/101588) . [Visit our website](http://www.apple.com) or contact your internet service provider (ISP) for more help.
-- Make sure that your security software or firewall allows access to [Apple software update servers](https://support.apple.com/en-us/101555#firewalls) .
+- Make sure that your firewall allows [access to our update servers](https://support.apple.com/en-us/101555#firewalls) .
-- [Configure or temporarily uninstall](https://support.apple.com/en-us/111760) your security software.
+- [Set up or temporarily uninstall](https://support.apple.com/en-us/111760) your security software.
-- Bypass your Internet router. Some routers might block iTunes from accessing the update server. Try the following:
+- Bypass your Internet router. Some routers might block iTunes from accessing the update server.
-- Disconnect from your wired or wireless router and use an Ethernet cable to connect your computer directly to your modem.
+- Disconnect from your wired or wireless router.
-- Restart your computer and modem. Contact your Internet service provider for instructions on using your modem.
+- Connect your computer to your modem using an Ethernet cable.
-After you confirm your Internet connection is working, try to [update](https://support.apple.com/en-us/118575) or [restore](https://support.apple.com/en-us/118107) your iOS or iPadOS device again.

+- Contact your ISP for instructions on using your modem.
+
+After you confirm your Internet connection is working, [update](https://support.apple.com/en-us/118575) or [restore](https://support.apple.com/en-us/118107) your iOS or iPadOS device again.
-Try to restore or update on another computer with a different Internet connection. Trying this helps to make sure there aren't issues with your computer that might stop it from communicating with the update server.
+Restore or update on another computer with a different Internet connection. This helps you rule out issues with your computer that might block communication with the update server.

For example, if you're restoring at work, try to restore at home or on a friend's computer and network.
